Subject: Request: Solaris commercial risk & discount — exec sign-off request

Hi Marissa, Laura —

Solaris pushed for a pilot start in mid-Nov and they've come back with substantive redlines (attached). Highlights: they want the standard liability cap moved from $1M to $10M, remove the IP carve-out from the indemnity clause, and extend warranty remedies to 180 days. Commercial is asking for a one-time 25% pilot discount in exchange for faster billing and a 12-month committed pilot.

Key constraints: Solaris needs an answer this week to hit onboarding dates. If we can't land a path, they will pause. Legal flagged this as high-risk and recommended exec sign-off for the liability and indemnity asks.

Attachments: Solaris_redlines_v3.docx, SOW_Solaris_Draft.pdf

As this sits in my queue, I need an exec decision on:
- liability cap increase (requested $10M)
- indemnity carveout removal
- warranty term extension
- commercial concession (they want 25% off pilot)

Recommended commercial compromise (my view): accept a capped increase to $5M tied to fees (2x expected 12-month fees) + limit warranty to 90 days and keep IP carveout intact. Offer 20% pilot discount instead of 25% and tighten onboarding SLA.

Ask: Marissa / Laura — can one of you approve escalating to CFO/CEO level for the liability cap or provide direction? Time-sensitive.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Michael —

Quick note from counsel: the redlines as drafted by Solaris remove/remap several of Redwood's standard protections. The three items you called out are the main risk drivers: (1) unlimited/very high liability exposure; (2) waiver of IP carveouts undermines our product IP protection; (3) extended warranty window increases potential remediation surface.

If Redwood is willing to move the liability cap, I recommend a structured cap tied to consideration (for example: greater of $X or 2x paid fees) with a hard upper bound and carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For the indemnity, keep IP-related obligations limited to willful infringement claims not routine performance bugs. For warranty, 90 days is reasonable — 180 days is high for this product profile.

I have attached a countermarkup (Counterterms_Redwood_v2.docx) that reflects these positions. If you want, I can join a call with your team and Solaris legal to walk through the redlines.

Katherine Lin
Senior Counsel, Barrister LLP (external counsel)

I've reviewed the proposed commercial trade-offs and risk framing. Finance is comfortable with a structured liability cap at $5M provided the following controls are in place:
- Cap = greater of $5M or 2x actual paid Redwood fees in the first 12 months (whichever is higher), but never exceeding $5M.
- Maintain IP carveout in indemnity; limit indemnity to willful infringement & security incidents where Redwood is legally liable.
- Warranty limited to 90 days with defined remediation SLAs.
- Accepted discount: 20% max for pilot when Solaris commits to 12-month purchase and monthly usage reporting; any further discount requires CFO/CEO approval.

I approve proceeding to present that counter to Solaris. If their legal pushes back on the cap structure, escalate to CEO for final authority.

Rishi Malhotra

Subject: RE: Request: Solaris commercial risk & discount — exec sign-off request (approved terms)

Teresa / Mark — thanks for your patience. Per internal review and counsel input, Redwood can accept a limited set of changes with the following counterproposal (approved by Sales leadership & Finance):

1) Liability cap: fixed cap of $5,000,000 (not to exceed) for covered direct damages. Cap is the upper bound; it is not unlimited.
2) Fee linkage: language that liability is calculated subject to an offset tied to paid fees (model: cap limited to greater of $5M or 2x paid Redwood fees in the first 12 months) — intent is protection for both sides.
3) Indemnity: maintain IP carveout — Redwood will indemnify for willful infringement and for liabilities arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; we cannot remove IP carveouts for routine bugs or product usage.
4) Warranty: limited to 90 days with agreed remediation SLAs.
5) Commercial concession: 20% pilot discount (not 25%), conditional on 12-month commit and monthly usage telemetry sharing.

Attachments: Counterterms_Redwood_v2.docx (redline), SOW_Solaris_Draft.pdf
Next steps: please confirm acceptance by EOD Friday 23 Oct so we can finalize DocuSign. I will push the counters to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-solaris-counter 

If Solaris requires changes to the cap structure beyond this proposal, Redwood will need final sign-off from our CEO.

Looking forward — happy to set a short call to walk through the redline.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
